Choose which department to attend and have an overnight sleep study in hospital or with a borrowed home device
If moderate or severe, wear a CPAP machine at night
Persist with the mask every night despite weeks of discomfort (many take it off after a few hours)
Buy the CPAP machine yourself, a considerable expense (China-specific market rule)
Diagnosis needs sleep monitoring, not a questionnaire alone
Wear CPAP for daytime alertness; RCTs did not show it prevents heart disease or death
People with no snoring and no daytime sleepiness need not seek testing (screening of symptom-free people unclear)
When sleepy while driving, stop the car first and rest (cross-reference to chapter 1 item 9)

findings.text: Nie próbuj samodzielnie dobierać aparatu CPAP ani jego ustawień.
findings.why: The item forbids the reader to choose or adjust CPAP but gives no route for the reader who has CPAP prescribed and struggles with it. The upstream states that adherence is the hard part (nightly mask, weeks of discomfort, many remove it after hours) and the Koszt field lists no effort cost at all. The cited NICE snapshots show that a route exists (contact the sleep service for advice, support and equipment; alternatives when CPAP is not tolerated), but the item says none of it. A reader prescribed CPAP may quietly stop using it, and for a person who was sleepy at the wheel that removes the very treatment the item describes.

evidence.text: 难在坚持：每晚都要戴着面罩睡，头几周不习惯，不少人戴几个小时就摘了。
Offer people with OSAHS having CPAP access to a sleep service for advice, support and equipment between follow-up appointments.
how to get support for technical and clinical problems, including side effects, and obtain replacement masks and other parts
If a person with moderate or severe OSAHS is unable to tolerate or declines to try CPAP

findings.fix_direction: Name the effort of nightly CPAP use as a cost, and pair the prohibition with a path (take problems back to the treating team or sleep service) limited to what the NICE snapshots support. Do not describe Polish service structure unless a verified Polish source is added.

findings.text: Zgłoś zauważone przerwy w oddychaniu, nasilone chrapanie lub nadmierną senność.
findings.why: The item gives three alternative triggers (any one is enough). The NICE recommendation cited in Korzyść i dowody#1 triggers assessment at 2 or more listed features. The upstream also states a scope limit (people with no snoring and no daytime sleepiness need not seek testing) that the item drops. Reporting one symptom to a doctor is low-risk, but the NICE sentence reads as backing a single-symptom trigger it does not state.

evidence.text: Take a sleep history and assess people for OSAHS if they have 2 or more of the following features:
所以不打鼾、白天也不困的人，不必专门去查。

findings.fix_direction: Either mark the any-single-symptom trigger as the item's own cautious wording, or align the trigger with what NICE says. The symptom-free scope limit comes from a source not stored among the snapshots (USPSTF is only named in the upstream span), so it cannot be restored as verified.

findings.text: Wytyczne NICE NG202 zalecają ocenę objawów i badania snu przy podejrzeniu obturacyjnego bezdechu sennego.
findings.why: The population word is lost. The NICE guideline is titled for over 16s, and the upstream sources are adult guidelines. The item never says who the advice is for, while the README says health information concerns adults in the stated scope. A parent could apply a statement about adult assessment and CPAP to a child.

evidence.text: Obstructive sleep apnoea/hypopnoea syndrome and obesity hypoventilation syndrome in over 16s
Clinical Practice Guideline for Diagnostic Testing for Adult Obstructive Sleep Apnea

findings.fix_direction: State the population (adults, or over 16 as the NICE title says) where the guideline is first cited.

findings.text: B — wytyczne kliniczne dotyczące diagnostyki i leczenia, bez jednej prognozy korzyści dla czytelnika.
findings.why: Letter B is justified for the two NICE sentences in Korzyść i dowody (published narrow conclusions of a clinical guideline). But the grade line is the only grade statement for the whole item, and two of the three action sentences in W praktyce (stop driving and choose another way to travel; do not self-select CPAP) are operational or editorial instructions. Per the README those are C-type. The only snapshot line behind the driving rule is a generic line in an insomnia page. B therefore hides that part of the advice has no guideline behind it.

evidence.text: do not drive when you feel sleepy

findings.fix_direction: Say in Ocena dowodów or W praktyce which sentences are guideline-backed and which are editorial or operational precautions.

findings.text: Jeśli czujesz senność podczas prowadzenia, nie kontynuuj jazdy; wybierz bezpieczne zatrzymanie i inny sposób podróży.
findings.why: The source is labelled 'NHS: senność i prowadzenie', but the linked page is the NHS insomnia page. It supports only one bullet in a self-help list. 'inny sposób podróży' appears in neither snapshot nor the upstream span (the upstream says only stop and rest). The extension is not marked as editorial, and the source label promises more than the page holds.

evidence.text: do not drive when you feel sleepy

findings.fix_direction: Label the source as the NHS insomnia page and mark the advice to choose another way to travel as an editorial precaution.

findings.text: Nie obiecujemy określonego spadku liczby wypadków ani ochrony przed zawałem lub zgonem.
findings.why: No stored snapshot says anything about crashes, heart events or mortality, so the sentence is neither supported nor contradicted by them. The upstream span (a lead only) reports that randomised trials did not show CPAP preventing heart disease or death and that it is worn for daytime alertness. The item softens a negative finding into 'we do not promise' and, in Korzyść i dowody, never states what treated readers gain, so a reader may keep hoping for heart protection.

evidence.text: 但试验没看出它能防心脏病、能让人少死，戴它是为了白天清醒

findings.fix_direction: Say what the cited guidelines cover (assessment and treatment pathway) and state plainly that these sources do not show a heart or survival benefit, but only if a verified source for that is added. Do not present the upstream trial results as checked.

findings.why: The figure 70% is in no snapshot; it is only in the upstream span, so it is a lead. The change note repeats it in a reader-facing field and calls it a 'promise', while the upstream presents it as an estimate (RR 0.3) from before-and-after comparisons, which the upstream itself says are not randomised. A skimming reader can take away '70% fewer accidents'.

evidence.text: 戴呼吸机后，白天的困劲明显减轻，开车出事少约七成
车祸那组数字来自治疗前后对比，不是随机分组

findings.fix_direction: Describe the removed claim without repeating the figure, or describe it accurately as an uncontrolled before-and-after estimate in the original.

findings.why: The condition is never explained. The upstream gave a plain-language definition (breathing repeatedly stops or becomes shallow during sleep) that was dropped, and the NICE page defines the syndrome. 'NICE' and 'NG202' are not identified as British guidance, although the page itself refers to UK bodies, so a reader in Poland is not told the sources are foreign. 'lekarzowi' does not say which doctor to approach first.

evidence.text: the upper airway is narrowed or closes during sleep when muscles relax
guidance from the Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA) and the UK government
睡眠呼吸暂停是睡着后呼吸一阵阵停住或变浅，人会憋醒，白天就犯困

findings.fix_direction: Explain the term on first use, say that NICE is a British body, and name the first-contact doctor only in terms the stored sources support.

findings.text: Przy takich objawach ważniejsze jest ustalenie przyczyny niż próba maskowania senności kawą.
findings.why: Coffee as a way of masking sleepiness is addressed by no snapshot and not by the upstream span. The only coffee line in the snapshots is about avoiding it before bed. The sentence is also not an assessment of cost versus benefit (the upstream had a benefit rating of medium and a stated reason), so the field does not do what AGENTS.md assigns to Ocena redakcyjna. Whether caffeine helps is outside the given texts and is not asserted here.

evidence.text: do not smoke or drink alcohol, tea or coffee at least 6 hours before going to bed

findings.fix_direction: Replace with an editorial cost-benefit judgement that rests on the stored sources, or remove the coffee comparison.

notes: No blocker found: no Chinese institution, number or legal rule appears in a reader-facing field except the change note (finding Zmiany w adaptacji); the only legal statement is the disclaimer that Polish driving-licence procedure is not described. Recency was run and found nothing: NICE NG202 snapshot shows Published 20 August 2021 and the NHS page last reviewed 19 March 2024, and they do not disagree; I did not assess from memory whether newer guidance exists. All three cited sources are British; no Polish or EU source is among the snapshots, and whether Polish practice differs is not decidable from the given texts. Convention used for preservation.fallback_stated: true = the reader still has a path or none is needed; false = the reader's path is lost. Protocol: I opened only the role file, AGENTS.md, README.md (Grep for the heading, then Read of lines 42-71, which runs about 13 lines past the end of the Jak czytać dowody section into the next section), the packet and the three named snapshots. CLAUDE.md was injected by the harness, not opened by me. Nothing under book/, tests/, tools/, the manifest, other snapshots, git history or chapter files was opened.
